title: The union blocks a staff band job; transposing tunes overnight in a Harlem hotel
summary: Brunswick tried to hire his band as staff but the union refused; he recalls transposing Chick Bullock's tunes overnight at a hotel.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: And they wanted to hire my band for staff band and the union wouldn't let them do it. They did everything they could to try to put it.
From out of town they tried to keep you from working.

Yeah, well they did, you see, because they even, they were so sure they was going to hire us to the Brunswick people rented an apartment for us for one year. Oh really? They took a lease out on it. And they fixed up the contracts and everything for us to sign and they called in the delegate from the union and the man told them, say, well no you can't do that. Say that's the same as a regular job. Say now if you go through with this they'd have to stop the other bands from recording further.

And they did everything. They tried to put us all in the union, you know, without the transfer. We'd see we was working on the transfer. Then they tried to, I don't know, they tried to do everything to get us in there. But they couldn't do it. They told us we still would have to be there six months before we could, they could hire us as a staff band. See, because they had some band there, the reason was for that. The band that they had there as their staff band was a band who they claimed took so long to learn those tunes. And they gave us a full tune for Chick Bula and they just gave us the lead of it and we got the keys what he was singing in. See, and we had to transfer from the original keys to that. So we went in the hotel at night and we transferred all of them and we ran over in the lap and the hotel had a piano. And so that next day, that next day we went down there and we knew them. They didn't say anything to us about them.
Which hotel was that by the way? Is that one up on 126th Street? I remember musicians used to say that. Where were you? Yeah, that's where it was.
Near the Apollo Theater. That's right.
I forgot the name of it.
I know how it is. Let's see what the name of that. Is it Braddock maybe?
Braddock Hotel? No, no, no. No, I can't think of the name.
I think that, I can't call the name of it.
I was thinking most hotels would kick you out and start in practicing.
Well, these people liked it, you know. Yeah. They're used to musicians. Yeah. Well, we quit. So we got, we went back there that next night, that next night when we come in and we got
